vintage.bps: Census Building Permits Survey annual state and county files, average of 2022, 2023, and 2024
vintage.fhfa: FHFA All-Transactions state index, 2000=100, through the latest year in the March 2026 workbook vintage
vintage.pep: Census population estimates, July 1 2020 to July 1 2024

national.note: Unit-weighted national Building Permits Survey valuation per unit, 2022-2024 average. State cost indexes are state unit value divided by these anchors, shrunk toward 1 when the cell is thin.

counties.name: Lower Connecticut River Valley Planning Region

tier1.source: Connecticut CAMA and Parcel Layer, services3.arcgis.com Connecticut_CAMA_and_Parcel_Layer
tier1.area_field_note: Land_Acres is rounded to integers in this layer, so bins use Shape__Area, which matches square-foot magnitudes (mean near one acre).

tier1.source: Hawaii Statewide TMKs (MapServer layer 25) and State Land Use Districts (layer 20) on geodata.hawaii.gov ParcelsZoning.
tier1.area_field_note: The parcel layer has no normalized zoning class. The binding tier-1 fact used by the model is the State Land Use Urban share of land. Housing eligibility uses geography_eligible_share, the assumed share of the single-family stock inside that district.

tier1.source: Utah Housing Unit Inventory, services1.arcgis.com HousingUnitInventory. Urban-county derivative of assessor parcels, not the full statewide SGID parcel layer.
tier1.area_field_note: Mean single-family lot is 0.512 acres. Feasibility uses a documented lognormal tail because the service did not return percentile bins in this build.

tier1.source: Wisconsin Statewide Parcels DB V1200 (2026), services3.arcgis.com Wisconsin_Statewide_Parcels_DB. Improved PROPCLASS 1 (residential) with GIS acres.
tier1.area_field_note: Class 1 is residential, not detached single-family only. The model caps eligible homes at the ACS single-family stock so apartments inside Class 1 are not treated as ADU lots.
